at: She folds her apron and wraps her shoes in it
alt: In a small palace room by one lamp, Dohwa wraps her shoes in her apron to go home at dawn, smiling with relief; behind her the paper door glows faintly from a lamp in the corridor.
scene: Intimate low three-quarter shot in a small bare palace room at night. FOREGROUND sharp: the one oil lamp on the floor, its flame close to the lens. Dohwa (young woman in plain white commoner hemp, hair simply pinned) kneels on the floor folding her apron around a pair of worn straw shoes, a small relieved half-smile, eyes down on the bundle, alive and unafraid. BEHIND her, soft and out of focus, the closed paper lattice door, and on the far side of the paper a faint warm glow of a lamp approaching down the corridor, just beginning, not yet a shape. Quiet dread under a gentle moment. Lamp raking her face and the folds of the apron from below; the walls fall into umber dark. No other person visible.

at: At first light they let her go home, as promised.
alt: At first light Dohwa walks home the long way through the opening market, barefoot, shoes in her hand, apron tied on wrong, while Saryang ward watches.
scene: Wide-to-medium low shot down a narrow market lane of thatched and tiled stalls at grey first light, mist in the lane. Dohwa walks toward the lens, barefoot in the mud, holding her straw shoes in one hand, her apron tied on wrong, hair come loose, face pale and set, eyes fixed straight ahead, refusing to look at anyone. A step behind her a palace steward in a dark robe walks with his hands in his sleeves. On both sides, stallkeepers opening shutters stop and stare, a woman turns her face away, a man whispers to another; they dissolve into soft mist and lamp bokeh. FOREGROUND: a blurred hanging basket at the edge of a stall. Cold, quiet, humiliating; no violence shown.
